controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body color at its measured dayside temperature, 3,100 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of HAT-P-7 b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 8 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

controls.label: Spitzer
controls.qualification: Published fit · Bell et al. (2021) · a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 60021, first published by Wong et al. (2016)) · longitude only
controls.notes: Brightness temperature at 4.5 µm of HAT-P-7 b from Bell et al. (2021)'s published fit to a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 60021, first published by Wong et al. (2016)). Their Fourier series becomes a map of longitude through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, so there is no north-south detail and every latitude is drawn alike. The hottest longitude is 57° west of noon. The false color runs from 2,200 to 3,250 K. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of HAT-P-7's planets in this map from above, to scale, with HAT-P-7 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

HAT-P-7 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (75, 81, 82) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 424865156, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 16-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
